title: China is ready to address AI risks, just not on US terms
key_facts: The Straits Times opinion column's standfirst says Beijing wants an equal seat at the AI standards-setting table.

It opens with China's response to a much-discussed essay on AI safety by Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei, which described AI's potential, its grave risks and a race between democratic and authoritarian regimes.
On 14 Sep, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun called 'fearmongering, confrontation and vicious competition' a hindrance to sound global AI governance.
The photo caption mentions Trump and Xi touring the National Archives Museum in Washington on Sept 25.
quote_evidence: Beijing wants an equal seat at the AI standards-setting table.
Fearmongering, confrontation and vicious competition will only hamper efforts towards sound global AI governance, which serves no one’s interest.
why_it_matters_hint: The column claims China will cooperate on AI risk only as an equal in standard-setting; the argument itself was not readable.
event_date: Column published 11 Oct 2026; Foreign Ministry remarks 14 Sep 2026.
notes: Only the opening could be read; everything past the second paragraph is unknown. Opinion.
